profile.headline: Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary: I have over 10 years of experience leading (both as a manager and technical lead) software teams to deliver cutting-edge user experiences for consumer electronic products. I enjoy researching and developing new modes of human/computer interaction and form factors. At HP I developed improved touch and trackpad experiences for Windows laptops, and contributed to the launch of a new projective form factor (HP Sprout). At Olio I led a team to customize Android (AOSP) to run on one of the first smartwatches with a round display.  At Google I led the development of the local search experience for Google Assistant Driving Mode, a multi-modal experience optimized for hands-free interaction with your phone while driving. I'm currently one of the tech leads for Google's Fitbit experience on Wear.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer
positions.locationName: San Diego, California, United States · Hybrid
positions.description:
Fitbit on Wear OS:
  A Tech Lead on the Fitbit on Wear OS application. Formed and led the infrastructure team, which sets the foundations of the overall application architecture, improves system health, and sets coding best practices for the team of 30+ engineers. Fitbit on Wear powers the health and fitness on the Pixel Watches. I was involved in the launch of all generations of Pixel Watches, including owning the Fitbit login and sync experience on the watch.

Google Assistant on Android Auto/Driving Mode:
  Technical Lead of the project to optimize the Google Assistant Local Search experience for Driving Mode. Driving Mode was a product that takes over your Android phone experience to provide a set of UI and voice controls that are optimized for driving. The Local Search experience provided a multi-modal UI (visual cards and voice cues) to find and navigate to nearby places. This was a server-driven UI, and I led a team of 3 engineers to build the server and mobile components of the experience.

positions.title: Technical Lead Manager
positions.description:
Google Maps Platform
  Tech Lead Manager (TLM) of the On-Demand Rides and Deliveries Consumer SDK. Led a team of 8 mobile engineers (Android and iOS) to build an mobile SDK on top of the Google Maps SDK. The Local Rides and Deliveries product was a platform tailored towards ride-sharing, delivery, and logistics companies that want to make use of Google's mapping technologies. The Consumer SDK enabled these companies to easily build a user experience for customers to view the real-time location of their driver or deliveries. Many on-demand companies around the world have successfully launched products using the library.

positions.title: Director, Software Architecture
positions.description: Skills: Embedded Linux · Wearable Technology · Android

positions.title: Director of SW Engineering, Co-founder
positions.description: Led Team to develop custom wearable OS based on AOSP. Gained familiarity with device bring-up including U-boot, Linux device drivers, and HAL library development. Managed the implementation of the manufacturing software including device flashing protocols, PCBA, and Finished good testing. Led development of custom Android services and applications involving many common Android design patterns such as content providers, custom View groups, loaders, and adapters
positions.insights: Skills: Embedded Linux · Wearable Technology · Android Framework · Android

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Joined a new product development team in the Advanced Platforms Group
Worked on a software team developing an SDK for a new product platform from HP (Sprout)
Exposed to Agile methodology, continuous integration, and unit testing practices
Interfaced with product management, UI designers, firmware/hardware team, and application developers
Coded in all levels of Windows development from drivers and C++, to .NET C#.

positions.title: Electrical/Hardware Engineer
positions.description:
Created and evangelized an innovative trackpad gesture system (HP ControlZone):
Developed initial prototypes, presented concept to management and executives, gained feedback from industrial and user experience designers, filed for patents, and kicked off development with our hardware partners.

One of a small group of engineers selected out of thousands to present at TechCon, HP's annual technology conference for leading engineer within the company. Presented a prototype of software I developed for improving trackpad user interaction. Filed patents related to the technology.

positions.title: Intern in Desktop Innovation and Incubation Group
positions.description:
Led project to investigate and test new technologies in the industry (including wireless 
charging, gesture recognition, and touchscreen technologies) 

Planned and executed a project to develop gesture recognition software using image 
processing functions such as face detection, motion tracking, background subtraction, and depth from stereo. Consulted with HP Labs researchers. 

Designed a mobile product accessory using Pro/E CAD software. Printed a prototype using a 3D 
printer.

positions.title: Intern
positions.description:
Worked on team that develops X-ray tubes for CT scanners:
     
Wrote software to parse CT scanner log files, and input data into a database using SQL 
     
Contacted field engineers to provide support and gain feedback on products 
    
Ran verification tests on high voltage connectors (140 kV). Completed testing documentation. 
     
Led project to switch a supplier of parts used in the manufacturing process 
     
Gained exposure to Lean, Six Sigma, and experienced an FDA mock audit.

positions.title: Student Computer Consultant
positions.description: Worked for the University of Virginia’s IT department, providing support at call centers, and walk-in help desks.

educations.schoolName: Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology

patents.title: System and method for automatic third party user interface adjustment
patents.description: A method for enabling a third party to dynamically reskin information displayed at a primary user device associated with a user account includes: transmitting a user interface template to a third party device, receiving assets from the third party device, delivering a bundle to a user device, and presenting the user interface based on the bundle.
